acceptance: codesign, spctl, notarization log, stapler validation, fresh install, and update tests pass.
observed: This is a repair of the prior MBR-901 pass (commit 2d543114), which shipped a bespoke codesign/notarytool/stapler pipeline duplicating signing RightKit already performs. Adrian clarified RightKit already provides proper signing on both macOS and Windows and is already wired into apps/membrane-hub (right-release.config.mjs targets.mac: signed:true, package: pnpm run rightkit:package:mac, artifacts: the DMG). The canonical build/sign/notarize path is now `pnpm release:doctor` then `pnpm release:build:mac` (right-release build --platform mac), which runs apps/membrane-hub/scripts/build-mac-release.mjs (tauri build --bundles app,dmg -- codesigns crypt-service, the membrane sidecar, and Membrane Hub.app inner-to-outer with hardened runtime, using the identity in tauri.conf.json; xcrun notarytool submit --wait; xcrun stapler staple/validate on the DMG; spctl -a -vv Gatekeeper assessment of the DMG), then RightKit's hardeningscan.mjs over the artifacts, then build-release.mjs's seal step (.right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<commit8>/mac/release-manifest.json binding the DMG's sha256). packaging/macos/release-contract.json and packaging/macos/bundle-manifest.json (the prior pass's bespoke signing-order contract) were deleted: nothing in this repository computes a codesign plan or runs codesign/notarytool/stapler as a mutating action anymore -- Tauri and RightKit already own that end to end. scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs was rewritten to drop validateReleaseContract/validateBundleManifest/signingOrder entirely and now (a) keeps the platform-acceptance receipt builder (buildPlatformAcceptanceReceipt/validatePlatformAcceptanceReceipt, reusing scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs unchanged -- this receipt type is membrane-specific evidence RightKit has no equivalent for, since RightKit seals artifacts but does not attest install/startup/update/uninstall lifecycle outcomes), (b) reads back RightKit's own sealed release-manifest.json (readSealedReleaseManifest, verifySealedInstallerHash, sealedReleaseDir) so the acceptance layer verifies RightKit's real sealed output, not a bespoke substitute, and (c) mirrors (does not import -- see below) @rightkit/release/notary-auth.mjs's notarytoolAuthArgs() so notarization-log evidence capture authenticates identically to the real build. scripts/release/macos/release-macos.mjs was rewritten: the `sign`, `notarize`, `staple`, and `plan` commands (all of which duplicated RightKit/Tauri actions) were deleted outright. `verify` now runs only read-only checks against what RightKit already produced -- codesign --verify --deep --strict, the hardened-runtime flag check, spctl --assess on the .app, hdiutil verify + spctl --assess on the DMG, and xcrun stapler validate on both (validate reads an existing ticket, it never staples one) -- and, when --sealed-dir is given, cross-checks the --dmg bytes against RightKit's sealed manifest hash. `notarization-log` is the one genuinely missing piece: RightKit's build submits and waits for notarization but never persists the submission ID or a durable log, so this command runs `xcrun notarytool log <submission-id>` and writes it to a confined path -- the notarization-log evidence this task's acceptance criterion names. `receipt`/`verify-receipt`/`platform-receipt` are functionally unchanged from the prior pass (same schemas, same downstream consumption by scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs, MBR-904, and MBR-808), only now built from the same read-only check suite as `verify` instead of a bespoke sign+notarize+staple sequence. packaging/macos/entitlements.plist is kept (its empty <dict/> already matches Tauri's default of applying no custom entitlements, since tauri.conf.json does not reference it) with its header comment updated to record that status honestly instead of implying it drives a bespoke codesign loop that no longer exists. All 16 tests in scripts/release/macos/release-macos-pipeline.test.mjs pass, including new coverage that the removed sign/notarize/staple/plan commands are gone, that notarytoolAuthArgs matches RightKit's default profile and fails closed on a partial credential triplet, and that readSealedReleaseManifest/verifySealedInstallerHash correctly read and hash-check a fixture RightKit-shaped sealed release. Real acceptance -- an actual right-release build:mac run producing a Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime, notarized, stapled .app/.dmg and sealed manifest; a real notarytool submission and log; a fresh install on a clean macOS VM; and an update test -- requires a signing credential, a notarization credential, and a clean macOS VM, none of which were available or invoked during this task.

requires: A Developer ID Application signing identity available to the keychain, matching apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json#bundle.macOS.signingIdentity
A notarytool keychain profile named apple-dev-notary (Apple ID + app-specific password), or the APPLE_API_KEY_PATH/APPLE_API_KEY/APPLE_API_ISSUER App Store Connect API key triplet
A real `pnpm release:build:mac` (right-release build --platform mac) run from apps/membrane-hub producing a sealed .app/.dmg under .right-release/sealed/
A clean macOS VM for fresh-install and update-test lifecycle evidence
